_about: Employee-facing versions of every KB article, written from kb_articles.json (each attempt keeps the meaning of the article's own Attempt 1 / Attempt 2). They are loaded as a version of each article: approved automatically in development, left as drafts for a supervisor in production. When this file changes, articles nobody has edited get the new text as a new version; anything a person wrote is never replaced. Check app names (VPN app, Company Portal, meeting app) against your own tools before approving. who=you: the employee does it. who=it: only IT can do it, so the bot explains what happens next and routes the ticket.

KB-001.title: Reset your password yourself
KB-001.summary: You can reset your password yourself in about two minutes, as long as you can still get a code on the personal email or mobile number registered to your account.

steps: On the company sign-in page, select **Forgot my password** (or **Can't access your account?**).
Enter your work email address and type the characters in the picture, if it shows one.
Choose to get a code by **text** or **email** to your registered contact, then enter the 6-digit code. It's valid for 10 minutes.
Choose a new password: at least **12 characters**, not one of your last 5 passwords, and not containing your name.
Sign in to your **laptop** with the new password first (it needs the office network or VPN), then to email and other apps. On your phone, update the password in your mail app when it asks.
attempt1.why: The code only goes to contact details already on your account, which proves it's really you without anyone else being involved. Signing in on the laptop first makes the new password reach everything else.

KB-002.title: Password reset with an identity check
KB-002.summary: I can reset your password for you once I've confirmed it's you with a sign-in approval on your registered authenticator app.
KB-002.handoff_message: **What happens next:** Identity Support will call you on your registered work number, check a couple of details to confirm it's you, and then reset your password with you on the call. Please have your laptop with you. For your safety, they'll never ask for your current password.

KB-003.title: Unlock your account
KB-003.summary: Your account locks itself for safety after 5 wrong passwords in a row. It's common, often caused by an old password saved on your phone or laptop, and I can unlock it once I've confirmed it's you.
KB-003.handoff_message: **What happens next:** Identity Support will confirm it's you, unlock your account and check what caused the lockout. A phone or laptop that still has your old password saved is the usual reason, so if you changed your password recently, update it in your phone's mail app or turn the phone's Wi-Fi off for now.

KB-004.title: Several password resets in a short time
KB-004.summary: Several password resets in a short time can be a sign that someone else is trying to get into your account, so I've paused further resets to protect you.
KB-004.handoff_message: **What happens next:** Security will review the recent sign-in attempts on your account and contact you shortly, usually within the hour. Please don't try another reset in the meantime. If you get a sign-in approval request on your phone that you didn't start, **deny it** and tell them.

KB-005.title: VPN won't connect
KB-005.summary: Sorry you can't get onto the VPN. Most of the time the VPN app is holding on to an old, half-closed connection, and a clean restart of the app fixes it.

attempt1.intro: Let's give the VPN app a clean restart:
steps: First check your internet works without the VPN: open any public website.
Disconnect the VPN, then close the VPN app completely: right-click its icon near the clock (you may need the **^** arrow) and choose **Exit** or **Quit**.
If the app's settings have **Clear cache**, **Reset** or **Clear saved credentials**, use it.
Open the VPN app again, connect, and approve the sign-in on your authenticator app when it asks.
Once it says **Connected**, open an internal site such as the intranet to check.
attempt1.why: Closing the app fully clears the stuck connection, so it builds a fresh one instead of retrying the broken one.

attempt2.intro: Let's set the VPN connection up again from scratch:
steps: In the VPN app's settings, remove the company connection (profile or portal address).
Open the **Company Portal**, find the **VPN profile** and choose **Install** (or **Reinstall**).
Restart your laptop. This also resets its network settings.
Connect again and approve the sign-in. If you see an error message or number, tell me exactly what it says.
attempt2.why: A damaged connection profile is the next most common cause, and reinstalling it replaces it cleanly. The restart clears Windows' network settings (the same effect as a network reset).

KB-006.title: VPN certificate or trust error
KB-006.summary: A certificate or 'untrusted server' error means your laptop can't confirm the VPN is genuine right now. The usual causes are an expired certificate on your laptop or the laptop's date and time being wrong.

attempt1.intro: First check the clock, then get a fresh certificate:
steps: Check the date, time and time zone at the bottom right of your screen. If they're wrong, go to **Settings → Time & language → Date & time**, turn on **Set time automatically**, and select **Sync now**.
Open the **Company Portal**, find the **VPN certificate** (or VPN profile) and choose **Reinstall**.
Close the VPN app completely, open it again and connect.
attempt1.why: Certificates only work within their valid dates, so a wrong clock makes a good certificate look expired. A fresh copy replaces one that really has expired.

attempt2.intro: Let's clear out the old certificate and repair the VPN app:
steps: If the VPN app's settings have an option to remove saved certificates, use it. If it needs admin rights, skip this step and tell me.
In the **Company Portal**, open the VPN app and choose **Repair** (or **Uninstall**, then **Install**).
Restart your laptop and connect again.
attempt2.why: An old certificate left behind can be picked instead of the new one, and a repair puts the app's own files back in order.

KB-007.title: VPN keeps dropping
KB-007.summary: A VPN that keeps disconnecting is usually caused by an out-of-date VPN app, the laptop going to sleep, or a weak or busy network.

steps: Update the VPN app: open the **Company Portal** and install any update for it, or use **Check for updates** in the app.
Stop the laptop sleeping while you work: **Settings → System → Power & battery → Screen and sleep**, and set **When plugged in, put my device to sleep after** to **Never**.
If you're on Wi-Fi, sit closer to the router, or use a network cable if you have one.
Reconnect and work as normal for half an hour.
attempt1.why: Newer versions of the app cope better with brief network blips, and sleep mode cuts the VPN off completely.

attempt2.intro: Let's find out whether it's the network:
steps: Connect your laptop to a different network, for example your phone's hotspot.
Use the VPN for 20–30 minutes.
Tell me whether it still drops, and roughly how often.
attempt2.why: If it only drops on one network, the problem is that network (often home router settings or busy hotel Wi-Fi), not your laptop, and that tells the team exactly where to look.

KB-008.title: Set up the VPN for the first time
KB-008.summary: Setting up the VPN takes about ten minutes. You'll need to be signed in to your laptop, and have your authenticator app on your phone for the first connection.

attempt1.intro: Here's how to set it up:
steps: Open the **Company Portal** (search for it in the Start menu) and install the **VPN** app.
In the Company Portal, also install the **VPN profile**. If the app asks for a portal address instead, the profile adds it for you.
Open the VPN app, select **Connect**, sign in with your work email and password, and approve the request on your authenticator app.
When it says **Connected**, open the intranet or another internal site to check it works.
attempt1.why: The app, the company profile and your sign-in approval together prove your laptop is allowed onto the company network.

steps: In the **Company Portal**, open the VPN app and choose **Repair** (or **Uninstall**, restart, then **Install**).
Reinstall the **VPN profile** from the Company Portal too.
Connect again and approve the sign-in. If you see an error, tell me exactly what it says.
attempt2.why: A first install sometimes stops halfway, and a repair replaces any part that didn't finish.

KB-009.title: Request standard software
KB-009.summary: Most standard software (Zoom, Teams, Adobe Reader, 7-Zip, Notepad++ and similar) is already approved for everyone and you can install it yourself in a few minutes from the Company Portal. Please don't download a copy from the internet: it won't be licensed or kept up to date.

attempt1.intro: Check the Company Portal first; if it's there, it's already approved for you:
steps: Open the **Company Portal** from the Start menu (on a Mac, from Applications).
Search for the software by name, for example **Zoom**.
If it's listed, select it and choose **Install**. Keep the laptop on and connected (office network or VPN) until it says **Installed**.
Open it from the Start menu and sign in with your **work account** (for Zoom, choose **Sign in with SSO** and enter your company's domain if asked).
If it **isn't** listed, or it says **Request** instead of Install, tell me and I'll ask the Software Asset team to assign it to you.
attempt1.why: Everything in the Company Portal is pre-approved and licensed for your role, so there's nothing to wait for.

attempt2.note: It isn't available to you in the Company Portal yet, so the Software Asset team will check it's approved for your role and assign a licence, usually **within a working day**. It then appears in the Company Portal, ready to install. If no licence is free, they'll move one from someone who no longer uses it or raise a purchase request, and tell you the expected date.

KB-010.title: Install software from the Company Portal
KB-010.summary: Most approved software installs itself from the Company Portal in a few minutes, with no admin rights needed.

steps: Open the **Company Portal** from the Start menu and search for the app.
Select it and choose **Install**. Keep the laptop on and connected (office network or VPN) until it says **Installed**; large apps can take 10–20 minutes.
If it asks you to restart, save your work and restart.
Open the app from the Start menu.
attempt1.why: The portal installs software the approved way, so it's licensed, configured for the company and kept up to date for you.

steps: Restart your laptop (this finishes any install that's waiting).
In the **Company Portal**, open the app and choose **Repair**, **Reinstall** or **Retry**.
If it fails again, tell me the exact error message or code shown in the Company Portal.
attempt2.why: A restart and a repair fix most half-finished installs without you losing your settings.

KB-011.title: Software licence expired or won't activate
KB-011.summary: When an app says its licence has expired or it can't activate, it's often just holding an old copy of your licence. Signing out and back in with your work account refreshes it, which fixes it in most cases.

steps: In the app, sign out: usually **Help → Sign out**, or your profile picture → **Sign out** (Adobe: **Help → Sign Out**; Microsoft Office: **File → Account → Sign out**).
Close the app completely, then open it again.
Sign in with your **work email** (not a personal account). If it asks for a licence key, choose **Sign in** instead.
Restart your laptop if it still shows the old message, then open the app once more.
attempt1.why: Company licences are attached to your work account, and signing in again makes the app fetch your current licence instead of the expired copy it kept.

attempt2.note: The licence needs looking at centrally. The Software Asset team will check your licence and reassign a free one, usually **within a working day**; if none is free, they'll check the renewal with procurement and tell you the expected date. If you need the software urgently, tell them, and they can look for a temporary option. Once it's done, sign out and back in to the app.

KB-012.title: Request new or non-standard software
KB-012.summary: Software that isn't in the Company Portal has to pass a security and licensing review before it can be installed. That protects your laptop and the company's data.
KB-012.handoff_message: **What happens next:** the review team checks the software's security, licence terms and cost, which usually takes **3–5 working days**. They may ask what you need it for and how many people will use it. Please don't download or install it from the internet in the meantime. If there's an approved alternative in the Company Portal, they'll suggest it.

KB-013.title: Hardware problem
KB-013.summary: Many hardware problems (a blank screen, a dock or monitor not working, a laptop running very hot or slow) come down to a cable, a connection or a stuck state, so let's rule those out before the hardware team gets involved.

steps: Save your work, then **restart** the laptop (Start → Power → **Restart**, not Shut down).
Unplug and firmly reconnect every cable: power, dock, monitor and USB. If you have a spare cable or charger, try it.
For a screen problem, press **Windows + P** and choose **Duplicate** or **Extend**; also try the laptop with the dock unplugged.
For overheating, put the laptop on a hard, flat surface (not a bed or lap) so the air vents are clear, and close apps you aren't using.
Please don't open the device or remove any covers.
attempt1.why: A restart clears a stuck state, and loose or faulty cables cause a large share of 'hardware' faults. If none of this helps, it's a real fault for the hardware team.

attempt2.note: This needs a hands-on check, so the **hardware team** will contact you to arrange a repair, a swap or a visit to the IT desk, and confirm the timing with you. They already have your device details and what you've tried. Save your work regularly in case it gets worse.

KB-013.handoff_message: **What happens next:** the hardware team will contact you to arrange a repair, a swap or a visit to the IT desk; they'll confirm the timing with you. Please don't open the device, and save your work regularly in case it gets worse.

KB-014.title: Laptop won't turn on
KB-014.summary: A laptop that won't turn on is often just completely out of charge or stuck, and these checks bring it back more often than you'd think.

steps: Plug the charger into a wall socket you know works (not an extension or dock), and check the charger's light or the laptop's charging light.
If you have another company charger, try that one.
Leave it charging for **15 minutes**: a completely flat battery shows nothing at first.
Unplug every accessory and the dock, then hold the power button for **20 seconds**, let go, and press it once normally.
If the lights come on but the screen stays black, connect an external monitor if you have one, or press **Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B**.
attempt1.why: Most 'dead' laptops have a flat battery, a faulty charger or a stuck power state, and the long press resets the power circuit without opening anything.

attempt2.note: This needs the **hardware team**, who will contact you to arrange a repair or a loan laptop so you can keep working. Your files saved in OneDrive or on the network are safe. If it was dropped or got wet, please tell them, and don't try to charge it.

KB-014.handoff_message: **What happens next:** the hardware team will contact you to arrange a repair or a loan laptop. If it was dropped or got wet, please tell them, and don't try to charge it.

KB-015.title: Keyboard, mouse or other accessory not working
KB-015.summary: When a keyboard, mouse, headset or dock stops working, it's very often the port, the batteries or the pairing rather than the device itself.

steps: **Wired:** unplug it and plug it into a **different USB port**, directly on the laptop rather than through the dock or a hub.
**Wireless:** replace or recharge the batteries, switch the device off and on, and plug its little USB receiver into a different port.
**Bluetooth:** open **Settings → Bluetooth & devices**, remove the device, then put it in pairing mode and select **Add device**.
**Dock:** unplug the dock's power for 30 seconds, plug it back in, then reconnect the laptop.
Restart the laptop and test again.
attempt1.why: Ports, batteries and pairing cause most accessory faults, and a direct connection shows whether the dock or the device is the problem.

attempt2.note: The accessory needs repairing or replacing, so the **hardware team** will arrange a replacement. In the office they'll tell you when to collect it from the IT desk; if you work remotely, they'll arrange delivery.

KB-015.handoff_message: **What happens next:** the hardware team will arrange a replacement. In the office they'll tell you when to collect it from the IT desk; if you work remotely, they'll arrange delivery.

KB-016.title: New phone: move your sign-in approvals
KB-016.summary: Moving your sign-in approvals to a new phone needs an identity check first. Then I'll clear the old registration so you can add the new phone in a couple of minutes.
KB-016.handoff_message: **What happens next:** Identity Security will call you on your registered work number to confirm it's you, then clear your old phone's registration and stay on the line while you set up the authenticator app on the new one. Have your laptop and the new phone with you.

KB-017.title: Sign-in approval not showing up
KB-017.summary: When the sign-in approval doesn't pop up, it's usually waiting inside the authenticator app, blocked by your phone's notification settings, or your phone's clock is slightly off.

steps: Open the **authenticator app** on your phone directly and pull down to refresh. The request is often waiting inside it.
If you're asked for a **number**, type the number shown on your computer screen into the app.

If you use the 6-digit code instead, make sure your phone sets its time automatically: **iPhone:** Settings → General → Date & Time → **Set Automatically**; **Android:** Settings → System → Date & time → **Set time automatically**.
Check notifications are allowed for the authenticator app, then try signing in again.
attempt1.why: Notifications sometimes don't appear even though the request has arrived, and the 6-digit codes only match if the phone's clock is exact.

attempt2.intro: Let's get you in with a backup code, then fix the app:
steps: On the sign-in screen, choose **Sign in another way** and use one of your **backup codes**.
Once you're in, open your account's **Security info** page, remove the authenticator entry, then choose **Add sign-in method → Authenticator app**.
Scan the QR code with the authenticator app on your phone and approve the test notification.
attempt2.why: A backup code gets you in once, and registering the app again repairs the link between your account and your phone.

KB-018.title: Outlook won't send or receive
KB-018.summary: When Outlook gets stuck, with emails sitting in the Outbox or nothing new arriving, a faulty add-in or a damaged Outlook profile is the usual cause. Your emails are safe on the server either way.

attempt1.intro: Let's test Outlook in safe mode, then give it a fresh profile if needed:
steps: Check you can open **Outlook on the web** (outlook.office.com) in your browser. If email works there, the problem is the Outlook app on your laptop.
Close Outlook. Hold **Ctrl** while you open it again, and choose **Yes** to start in safe mode. Try sending a test email to yourself.
If it works in safe mode, an add-in is the cause: go to **File → Options → Add-ins**, select **COM Add-ins → Go**, and untick the add-ins one at a time.

If it doesn't work in safe mode either, create a fresh profile: close Outlook, open **Control Panel → Mail → Show Profiles → Add**, sign in, then select **Always use this profile** and choose the new one.
Open Outlook and send yourself a test email. The first sync can take a few minutes.
attempt1.why: Safe mode switches off add-ins, the most common cause. A new profile replaces damaged settings without deleting anything, because your mail is stored on the server.

attempt2.note: The Messaging team will check your mailbox on the server, including whether it's full or blocked from sending. If it's full, they'll add space or help you archive. Until then you can use **Outlook on the web**.

KB-019.title: Missing emails or calendar not syncing
KB-019.summary: Emails that seem to disappear are usually moved by a rule or the Focused/Other filter, and a calendar that won't update usually needs a fresh sync.

attempt1.intro: Let's find them and refresh the sync:
steps: Search for a missing email by its sender, with **All mailboxes** selected in the search scope.
Check **Junk Email**, **Other** (next to Focused) and **Deleted Items**.
Open **File → Manage Rules & Alerts** and look for any rule that moves or deletes these emails; untick it if so.
Right-click the folder or calendar and choose **Update Folder** (or **Send/Receive → Update Folder**).
Compare with **Outlook on the web**: if the email or meeting is there, it's only your laptop's copy that's behind.
attempt1.why: Rules and filters quietly move email, and a re-sync fetches anything that didn't come through.

attempt2.note: Your laptop's local copy of the mailbox needs rebuilding, or the calendar needs reconnecting. The Messaging team will do this with you; it takes a little while to download everything again, but nothing is lost. **Outlook on the web** shows everything in the meantime.

KB-020.title: Access to a standard application
KB-020.summary: Standard business applications (Salesforce, Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow and similar) are granted from the approved access list for your role. Often you already have access and the app just hasn't picked it up, so let's check that first.

attempt1.intro: Check whether you already have it:
steps: Open **My Apps** (myapps.microsoft.com, or the apps launcher in Office 365) and look for the application. If it's there, open it from that tile.
If it's there but says **Access denied**, sign out of the app completely, close your browser, and sign in again with your work account. New access is only picked up at sign-in.
If it isn't in My Apps at all, select **Request access** there (or **+ Add apps**), choose the app and the role you need, and submit. Standard roles are approved automatically.
Tell me what happened, including any error message.
attempt1.why: Access is attached to your work account when you sign in, so a fresh sign-in picks up anything granted recently, and standard roles can be requested without waiting for anyone.

attempt2.note: The Application Access team will check your role against the approved access list and grant it, usually **within a working day**, or push through access that's been granted but hasn't reached the app yet. You'll get a notification when it's done; then sign out of the app and back in. If the role needs approval, they'll ask your manager for you.

KB-021.title: Admin or privileged access
KB-021.summary: Admin and other privileged access always needs approval, for everyone, because it can change systems or see sensitive data.
KB-021.handoff_message: **What happens next:** I've raised an approval request with the application owner, your manager and Security. They'll check what you need it for and may grant it for a limited time only. You'll be notified of the decision, usually within **2–3 working days**. If you only need one task done, the team may be able to do it for you sooner.

KB-022.title: No internet on the office Wi-Fi
KB-022.summary: When the office Wi-Fi shows connected but nothing loads, the saved connection on your laptop has usually gone stale, and reconnecting from scratch fixes it.

attempt1.intro: Let's reconnect to the Wi-Fi from scratch:
steps: Ask a colleague nearby whether their internet works. If it doesn't, tell me: it's likely a wider problem.
Select the Wi-Fi icon near the clock, right-click the office network and choose **Forget**.
Select the office network again and sign in with your work account if it asks.
Open a website to test.
attempt1.why: Forgetting the network clears saved settings that may have gone stale, so the laptop gets a fresh connection.

attempt2.intro: Let's refresh your laptop's network settings:
steps: Turn Wi-Fi **off**, wait 10 seconds, and turn it back **on**.
If that doesn't help, restart your laptop. This resets the network adapter and clears stored website addresses (the DNS cache).
Connect to the office Wi-Fi again and test.
attempt2.why: Restarting the adapter and clearing stored addresses gives the network connection a completely clean start.

KB-023.title: Websites won't load at home on the VPN
KB-023.summary: When some sites won't load at home while you're on the VPN (errors like 'This site can't be reached'), your laptop is usually using out-of-date website addresses (DNS).

steps: Disconnect the VPN and check the site loads without it. If nothing loads at all, restart your home router first.
Restart your laptop. This clears the stored website addresses (the DNS cache).
Connect to the VPN again and try the site.
attempt1.why: Your laptop may be looking sites up with old addresses, and a restart makes it fetch fresh ones through the VPN.

attempt2.note: The Network team will check how the VPN sends your traffic (split tunnelling) and the address settings for those sites. Please tell them **which sites** fail and whether they work with the VPN off.

KB-024.title: Suspicious or phishing email
KB-024.summary: Thanks for reporting it. Flagging a suspicious email quickly is exactly the right thing to do.
KB-024.handoff_message: **Until Security looks at it:** don't click links, open attachments or reply, and don't forward it to colleagues. If your mail app has a **Report phishing** button, you can use it too. Security Operations will check the message and remove copies from other mailboxes if it's malicious. **If you entered your password anywhere, tell me straight away.**

KB-025.title: Password entered on a suspicious page
KB-025.summary: Thanks for telling us quickly. Acting in the first few minutes makes a real difference.
KB-025.handoff_message:
**Right now:** treat that password as known to someone else. Don't use it anywhere, and if you use the same password for anything else, change it there too. If you get a sign-in approval on your phone that you didn't start, **deny it**.

**What happens next:** Security will contact you very soon to confirm it's you, reset your password and sign-in approvals, and check your account for any unusual activity.

KB-026.title: Printing is stuck
KB-026.summary: When documents sit in the queue and nothing prints, one stuck job is usually blocking everything behind it.

steps: Check the printer itself first: it's on, has paper and toner, and its screen shows no error.
On your laptop, open **Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners**, select the printer and choose **Open print queue**.
Select **⋯ → Cancel all** (or cancel each document).
Restart your laptop. This restarts Windows' printing service.
Print one page to test.
attempt1.why: One stuck document blocks everything behind it, and restarting clears the printing service's memory.

steps: In **Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners**, select the printer and choose **Remove**.
Add it again: select **Add device**, or install it from the **Company Portal** if your office lists printers there.
Print a test page. If it still fails, note the printer's name or number (on a sticker on the printer) and any error on its screen.
attempt2.why: Reinstalling puts a fresh driver on your laptop, which fixes printing that fails even with an empty queue.

KB-027.title: Printer shows as offline
KB-027.summary: A printer that shows as offline is often working fine; your laptop's printing service has just lost track of it.

steps: Check the printer is on and shows no error, and that you're on the office network (or the VPN).
In **Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners**, select the printer, open the print queue and make sure **Use printer offline** isn't ticked (under the **Printer** menu).
Restart your laptop. This restarts the printing service.
Print again.
attempt1.why: Restarting the printing service makes your laptop find the printer again on the network.

steps: In **Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners**, select the printer and choose **Remove**.
Add it again from the **Company Portal** (or **Add device**) so the latest driver installs.
Print a test page, and if it still says offline, tell me the printer's name or number.
attempt2.why: An old or damaged driver can make a working printer look offline.

KB-028.title: No sound or video in meetings
KB-028.summary: When others can't hear or see you (or you can't hear them), the usual causes are Windows blocking the microphone or camera, or the meeting app using the wrong device.

attempt1.intro: Let's check the permissions and devices:
steps: Open **Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone**: turn on **Microphone access** and **Let desktop apps access your microphone**. Do the same under **Camera**.
Check nothing is physically blocking the camera (a privacy shutter or cover) and that your headset isn't muted.
In the meeting app, open **Settings → Devices** (Teams) or **Settings → Audio/Video** (Zoom) and choose the right speaker, microphone and camera.
Make a test call: in Teams, **Settings → Devices → Make a test call**.
attempt1.why: Windows can block apps from the microphone and camera even when everything is plugged in, and meeting apps sometimes pick the wrong device after you plug in a headset or dock.

steps: Quit the meeting app completely: right-click its icon near the clock and choose **Quit**.
Reinstall it from the **Company Portal** (choose **Reinstall** or **Repair**).
Restart your laptop, open the app and make another test call.
attempt2.why: Old cached settings in the app can keep it pointing at the wrong device, and a fresh install clears them.

KB-029.title: Can't join a meeting
KB-029.summary: If the meeting app won't let you in, joining from your web browser usually works straight away, so you don't miss the meeting.

steps: Open the meeting invitation and copy the **join link**.
Paste it into **Microsoft Edge** or **Google Chrome** and choose **Continue on this browser** (Teams) or **Join from your browser** (Zoom).
Sign in with your work account if asked, and allow the microphone and camera when the browser asks.
If you're still stuck, you can usually **dial in** with the phone number in the invitation.
attempt1.why: The web version doesn't use the desktop app at all, so anything wrong with the app can't stop you joining.

attempt2.intro: Let's fix the desktop app for next time:
steps: Quit the meeting app completely: right-click its icon near the clock and choose **Quit**.
Reinstall it from the **Company Portal** (choose **Reinstall** or **Repair**), then restart your laptop.
Sign in to the app and join a meeting again. If it shows an error, tell me exactly what it says.
attempt2.why: A fresh install replaces damaged app files and cached sign-in details that stop it joining.

KB-030.title: Work phone setup or compliance problem
KB-030.summary: When your phone says it isn't compliant, or work apps like Outlook or Teams stop working on it, the work profile usually just needs to re-check and sync.

steps: Make sure your phone has the latest system update and a screen lock (PIN, fingerprint or face). These are the most common compliance checks.
Open the **Company Portal** app on your phone.
**iPhone:** tap **Devices → this device → Check status**. **Android:** tap **⋮ → Settings → Sync**, or **Check device settings**.
Wait a few minutes, then open the work app again.
attempt1.why: Syncing re-checks your phone against the company rules and refreshes the work profile, which fixes most compliance warnings.

attempt2.intro: Let's set up the work profile again:
steps: In the **Company Portal** app, remove this device (**Remove device** or **Remove company access**).
Enrol again in the Company Portal app and follow the steps. Your work apps and email come back on their own.
Your personal photos, apps and data aren't touched; only the work part is replaced.
attempt2.why: A fresh work profile replaces one that can no longer sync.

KB-031.title: Lost or stolen phone
KB-031.summary: I'm sorry your phone is lost. The quickest way to protect your work data is to lock or wipe it remotely. The device team does that once they've confirmed it's you, with Security's approval.
KB-031.handoff_message:
**While you wait:**
- If you can, use **Find My** (iPhone) or **Find My Device** (Android) from another device to see where it is or make it ring.
- Please don't erase it yourself; the team will remove company data properly.
- If it was stolen, report it to the police and keep the reference number.
